q-14553.name: Question 1
q-14553.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 4}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x-8}{{x}^{2}+x-20} & =\frac{{4}^{2}-2(4)-8}{{4}^{2}+4-20}=\frac{0}{0},\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x-8}{{x}^{2}+x-20} & =\frac{(x+2)(x-4)}{(x+5)(x-4)} \\  & =\frac{x+2}{x+5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 4}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x-8}{{x}^{2}+x-20} & ={lim}_{x\to 4}\frac{x+2}{x+5} \\  & =\frac{4+2}{4+5} \\  & =\frac{6}{9} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-101157.name: Question 2
q-101157.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -4}\frac{{t}^{2}-16}{{t}^{2}+4t} & =\frac{(-4)^{2}-16}{(-4)^{2}+4(-4)}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{t}^{2}-16}{{t}^{2}+4t} & =\frac{(t+4)(t-4)}{t(t+4)} \\  & =\frac{t-4}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to -4}\frac{{t}^{2}-16}{{t}^{2}+4t} & ={lim}_{t\to -4}\frac{t-4}{t} \\  & =\frac{-4-4}{(-4)} \\  & =\frac{(-8)}{(-4)} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

q-107041.name: Question 3
q-107041.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 5}\frac{{x}^{2}-5x}{{x}^{2}-8x+15} & =\frac{{5}^{2}-5(5)}{{5}^{2}-8(5)+15}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-5x}{{x}^{2}-8x+15} & =\frac{x(x-5)}{(x-5)(x-3)} \\  & =\frac{x}{x-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 5}\frac{{x}^{2}-5x}{{x}^{2}-8x+15} & ={lim}_{x\to 5}\frac{x}{x-3} \\  & =\frac{5}{5-3} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-140416.name: Question 4
q-140416.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{{x}^{3}-27}{2x-6} & =\frac{{3}^{3}-27}{2(3)-6}=\frac{27-27}{6-6}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. 

Notice that the numerator is a difference of cubes. Therefore, factoring our expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{3}-27}{2x-6} & =\frac{{x}^{3}-{3}^{3}}{2(x-3)} \\  & =\frac{(x-3)({x}^{2}+3x+{3}^{2})}{2(x-3)} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+3x+9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{{x}^{3}-27}{2x-6} & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{{x}^{2}+3x+9}{2} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{2}+3(3)+9}{2} \\  & =\frac{9+9+9}{2} \\  & =\frac{27}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
